Background Cancer remains a leading global cause of mortality, making early detection crucial for improving survival outcomes. The study aims to develop a machine learning-enabled blood-derived exosomal RNA profiling platform for multi-cancer detection and localization. Methods In this multi-phase, multi-center study, we analyzed RNA from exosomes derived from peripheral blood plasma in 818 participants across eight cancer types during the discovery phase. Machine learning techniques were applied to identify potential pan-cancer biomarkers. During the screening and model validation phases, the sample size was progressively expanded to 1,385 participants in two steps, while the candidate biomarkers were refined into a set of 12 exosomal tumor RNA signatures (ETR.sig). In the subsequent model construction phase, diagnostic models were developed using the expanded cohort and ETR.sig. Statistical analyses included the calculation of receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and AUC values to assess the models' ability to distinguish cancer cases from controls and determine tumor origins. To further validate and explore the biological relevance of the identified biomarkers, we integrated tissue RNA-seq, single-cell data, and clinical information. Results Machine learning analysis initially identified 33 candidate biomarkers, which were narrowed down to 20 ETR.sig in the screening phase and 12 ETR.sig in the validation phase. In the model construction phase, a diagnostic model based on ETR.sig, built using the Random Forest (RF) algorithm, showed excellent performance with an AUC of 0.915 for distinguishing pan-cancer from controls. The multi-class classification model also demonstrated strong classification power, with macro-average and micro-average AUCs of 0.983 and 0.985, respectively, for differentiating between eight cancer types. Additionally, tumor origin classification using the RF-based diagnostic models achieved high AUC values: BRCA 0.976, COAD 0.98, KIRC 0.947, LIHC 0.967, LUAD 0.853, OV 0.972, PAAD 0.977, and PRAD 0.898. Integration of tissue RNA-seq, single-cell data, and clinical information revealed key associations between ETR.sig-related genes and tumor development. Conclusions The study demonstrates the robust potential of exosomal RNA as a minimally invasive biomarker resource for cancer detection. The developed ETR.sig platform offers a promising tool for precision oncology and broad-spectrum cancer screening, integrating advanced computational models with nanoscale vesicle biology for accurate and rapid diagnosis. extracted_data.document_summary: This multi-phase, multi-center study developed and validated a machine learning-enabled blood-derived exosomal RNA profiling platform (ETR.sig) for noninvasive multi-cancer detection and localization, demonstrating its robust potential for accurate diagnosis, tumor origin classification, and prognostic assessment across eight primary cancer types.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic biomarker discovery and validation for multi-cancer detection and prognosis using exosomal RNA signatures.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This multi-phase, multi-center study involved a discovery phase (818 participants, 8 cancer types, 194 healthy controls, exoRNA-seq), a screening phase (245 participants, TaqMan qPCR), and a validation phase (1,385 participants). Machine learning (Random Forest and LASSO algorithms) was applied to refine 33 initial candidate biomarkers down to 12 exosomal tumor RNA signatures (ETR.sig). Diagnostic models were built with stratified random sampling (7:3 or 8:2 training/validation splits, tenfold cross-validation). Filtering criteria for differential gene expression included |log2FC|>1 and P<0.05 for bulk RNA-seq, and P<0.01 with FC ≥1.4 or ≤−1.6 for multi-cancer exoRNA-seq. The study focused on diagnostic development and biomarker identification, thus no therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Exosomal Tumor RNA signatures (ETR.sig) panel (including ALB, FCER1G, KRT18, LCN2, PPDPF, SLC9A3R2, AGO2, CKS2, MALAT1, RAB32, S100A9, UBE2Q2)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Exosomes derived from peripheral blood plasma; gene expression data from 15 cancer types (BLCA, BRCA, CESC, COAD, ESCA, HNSC, KIRC, KIRP, LIHC, LUSC, OV, PAAD, PEAD, SKCM, STAD) from TCGA and GEO databases for prognostic assessment.
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: RNA Profiling (exoRNA-seq, TaqMan qPCR), Gene set score.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly different expression and higher diagnostic score in cancer, demonstrating high diagnostic accuracy and strong classification power.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Achieved an AUC of 0.915 for multi-cancer diagnosis vs. controls, with macro-average AUC of 0.983 and micro-average AUC of 0.985 for differentiating eight cancer types. Tumor origin AUCs ranged from 0.853 (LUAD) to 0.98 (COAD). Kaplan-Meier survival curves showed P < 0.05 for significant differences in overall survival between high- and low-score groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects tumor presence, development, metastasis, and prognosis by mediating exosome-based RNA communication. Implicated in cancer-related pathways (e.g., cytokine-cytokine receptor, PI3K-Akt, ECM-receptor interaction) and impacts overall survival.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Multi-cancer detection, localization, and origin determination across eight specific cancer types (BRCA, COAD, KIRC, LIHC, LUAD, OV, PAAD, PRAD) and prognostic assessment across 15 cancer types.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A highly accurate, minimally invasive, and rapid diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for multi-cancer detection, localization, and risk assessment. It indicates advanced tumor stages, poorer prognoses, and specific cellular involvement within the tumor microenvironment (macrophages, epithelial cells, fibroblasts).
